catalog_quote: [Ferlus 1999 p.1] Toutes les langues du groupe vietique sont des langues tonales. Le ton se manifeste sur la voyelle de la syllabe principale du mot ... Le nombre des tons contrastifs peut aller de six (vietnamien, mường, cuối) à quatre (pong, sách/rục, thavung) quelle que soit la raison de cette réduction. [p.2] Les langues utilisées sont : 1 : maleng brô, mãliềng; 2 : arem; 3 : sách/rục (Nguyễn Vǎn Lợi 1993); 4 : thavung; 5 : pong, toum, liha; 6 : cuối; 7 : mường (Sokolovskaia & al. 1987), nguồn; 8 : vietnamien. ... Langues du sud : cuối : mɐ²; pong : kᵊma²; toum, liha : ma² ... [p.4] Les disharmonies du troisième type, quant à elles, ne dépendent pas de la structure syllabique. Elles se manifestent sur la syllabe accentuée (porteuse du ton dans le mot), que cette syllabe soit un monosyllabe ou la syllabe principale d'un dissyllabe. [Ferlus 1998 sec. 11] Système hétérodoxe à 4 tons: pong, toum. Le pong est parlé dans le district de Tương Dương, province de Nghệ An ... Le toum est parlé dans le district de Viang Thong, province de Bolikhamxay au Laos. - 4 tons dans les syllabes en finale sonore; - 2 + 2 tons dans les syllabes en finale sourde; - pas de -h final; - pas de voix soufflée ... [sec. 13] Ces systèmes à 4 tons caractérisent les langues et dialectes du sous groupe hung (pong ou phong, toum, liha)

new_statements.translation: [p.1] All languages of the Vietic group are tone languages. Tone is realized on the vowel of the main syllable of the word [...] The number of contrastive tones ranges from six (Vietnamese, Muong, Cuoi) to four (Pong, Sach/Ruc, Thavung) [...] [p.4] Disharmonies of the third type do not depend on syllable structure. They appear on the accented syllable (the tone-bearing syllable of the word), whether that syllable is a monosyllable or the main syllable of a disyllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Hung (Pong/Toum/Liha) is a tone language (4 tones per Ferlus 1998 sec. 11); words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (presyllable + main syllable, e.g. Pong kᵊma² 'rain'), and the accented, tone-bearing syllable is the main syllable, i.e. the final syllable of a disyllable; the presyllable carries no tone/accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None; statement is a family-wide generalization, not a Hung-specific rule with exceptions.
new_statements.domain_note: Word domain (lexical mono-/sesquisyllables). CAUTION: this is a Vietic-wide statement in a comparative/historical article by the fieldworker who collected the Pong, Toum and Liha data himself; no Hung-specific description of stress was found. The only detailed first-hand stress description filed under this glottocode by Glottolog (Enfield & Diffloth 2009: 'Any Kri word has one stressed syllable.. the final syllable receives full stress', pp.10-11, 27-28) is for Kri, which is a Maleng-group language, not Hung (see the note on which variety).
new_statements.identity_note: IDENTITY WARNING. All four Glottolog 5.1 descriptive refs for hung1275 describe KRI (Enfield & Diffloth), not Hung. Kri is spoken on the upper Nam Noy, Nakai, Khammouane (Laos); Enfield & Diffloth (2009: 7-8) say its closest relative/mutually intelligible neighbour is 'Phoongq' downstream and that Rivière's (1902) 'Harème' referred to the Kri. Ferlus 1996 (MKS 26: 12-13, 19) identifies Rivière's Harème and the Kha Phong (= 'Maleng kari') of the Nam Theun basin as the MALENG subgroup, explicitly distinct from the Pong/Phong of Tương Dương (Nghệ An) which is the Hung subgroup; Ferlus 1998 (p. 2) lists '1: mãliềng, maleng brô, kha phong (ou maleng kari)' vs '5-hung: pong (ou phong), toum, liha, đan lai'. Glottolog's own name index lists 'Kri' under Kha Phong khap1242 (dialect of Maleng male1282). So the Kri statement (fixed: final syllable stress, non-tonal register language) should be catalogued under Maleng male1282 / khap1242 (or as 'Kri, no own glottocode'), NOT under hung1275. The statement I give for hung1275 proper is Ferlus's family-level Vietic statement, whose stated scope includes pong, toum, liha (his own field data); Hung proper is a 4-tone language (Ferlus 1998 sec. 11: Pong of Tương Dương, Toum of Viengthong, Bolikhamxay).

Sec. 11 (HAL pp.14-15) 'Système hétérodoxe à 4 tons: pong, toum': Pong (Tương Dương, Nghệ An) and Toum (Viengthong, Bolikhamxay) have 4 tones on sonorant-final syllables, 2+2 on stop-final, no final -h, no breathy voice; tone values given. p.2 classification separates '1: mãliềng, maleng brô, kha phong (ou maleng kari)' from '5-hung: pong (ou phong), toum, liha, đan lai'.
